finalText:
This is almost always one of two things.

**The parent is handing over new objects or functions each time.** Even if the values look the same, `{}`, `[]`, and arrow functions you write inline are brand new each render. React checks if the prop is the exact same thing in memory, not if it looks the same — so it sees a change and re-renders the child.

**Or the child isn't set up to skip re-renders at all.** By default, a child re-renders whenever its parent does, no matter the props. Wrapping it in `React.memo` is what tells React "skip this one if the props really didn't change."

Two fixes, worth doing together:
1. Wrap the child in `React.memo(MyChild)`.
2. In the parent, keep any function or object props stable with `useCallback` or `useMemo`, instead of writing them fresh inline.

If you paste the parent and child code, I can point to the exact spot causing it.
